graders.name: clear-defaults
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Where a choice recurs it states the default, such as production via the read replica and a default time window (the notes use the last hour; a window around the alert also counts), and mentions alternatives only where they change what the agent does.

graders.name: coherent-unit
graders.criteria: Judge the new skill's files. They make one coherent investigation workflow, not a dump of every fact in the notes or general AWS or Postgres documentation.

graders.name: coined-terms-defined
graders.criteria: Judge the new skill's files. Any term the skill coins, one the notes and repo do not already use, is defined where it first appears. Pass if it coins none.

graders.name: commands-for-mechanical-steps
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Each mechanical step (searching logs, running a Logs Insights query and fetching its results, querying the database) gives a command the agent can run, with placeholders or named inputs for values that change per investigation, such as the time window, order or request IDs. Pass if no such step is left as prose only ("check the logs") without a command or a pointer to one.

graders.name: completion-criterion
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. It gives a checkable done-condition for the investigation, for example that the stated cause is backed by specific log lines or query results, or that what is still unknown is stated with the next check, rather than a vague "investigate thoroughly" or an artificial metric such as a minimum number of queries.

graders.name: description-out-of-body
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. The body does not repeat the description's trigger list; any activation or scope rules the description cannot carry are in a `## Boundaries` section.

graders.name: description-shape
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. The frontmatter `description` is quoted, under 1024 characters, written in the third person, and has two parts: a first sentence saying what the skill does using words a user would type (investigate, alerts, bugs, errors, logs, database), then a sentence saying when to use it.

graders.name: description-triggers
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. The description's trigger part names each distinct situation once (an alert from Slack or CloudWatch, a bug or support report, an error to explain) rather than piling up synonyms for one, and any exclusion it adds names a real near-miss, such as deploy reviews that `deploy-check` handles.

graders.name: frontmatter-fields
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. The frontmatter holds `name` and `description`, plus only optional fields that carry information for this skill; no placeholder or empty fields.

graders.name: grounded-in-notes
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Its investigation methods come from `docs/incidents/` and the repo: CloudWatch log group `/ecs/orders-api` searched with `aws logs tail` filter patterns and Logs Insights (`aws logs start-query` then `aws logs get-query-results`), and production data read through `scripts/db-ro.sh` (read replica, read-only role), including checks such as active queries and locks in `pg_stat_activity`, table constraints with `\d`, and order or payment rows. Pass if it keeps at least the log and database methods, naming the log group, script and checks or pointing to the repo file that states them (such as README.md), and invents no tools, log groups or access paths the notes and README do not show.

graders.name: inventory-updated
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/README.md`, which lists the project's skills. Pass if it now lists `investigate` with a one-line use.

graders.name: layout
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Pass if any supporting files it points to live one level deep in the skill folder (`references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) and are referenced by relative paths, or if the skill needs and points to none.

graders.name: leading-words
graders.criteria: Judge the new skill's files. They use the repo's own terms for recurring things (the log group, the read replica, an alert) and keep using the same word for the same thing. Naming the log group itself is not required.

graders.name: loads-not-copies
graders.criteria: Where the investigation needs what `deploy-check` covers, the new skill names `deploy-check` and when to use it rather than copying its steps. Pass if it never needs it.

graders.name: model-invoked
graders.description: An investigation skill the agent should pick up when an alert or bug report arrives stays model-invoked.

graders.name: name-matches
graders.description: The frontmatter name matches the directory.

graders.name: no-incident-history
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. It is a reusable workflow, not a record of past incidents: no incident narratives, dates, or people's names (Priya, Tomás, Marco). A lesson from an incident may appear as a check to run, such as checking table constraints when duplicates appear, without the story behind it.

graders.name: ordered-where-it-matters
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Steps that depend on each other are in order: establish what the alert or report says and the time window before querying, gather evidence before concluding, and report at the end. Steps that do not depend on each other are not forced into a fixed sequence or a rigid template beyond what a consumer needs.

graders.name: outcome-first
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Before the steps, it says what a finished investigation delivers, such as the cause or the most likely cause with the log and data evidence behind it, the impact, and a recommended next action.

graders.name: parameterized
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Values specific to one past incident (request `req_8f2c1e`, orders `ord_55120`, `ord_60031`, customer `cus_Q81`, account `acct_test_77`, ticket SUP-2291, epoch times 1785657600/1785661200, PR #812, the backfill job name) appear only as clearly marked examples or not at all; commands use placeholders for them.

graders.name: plain-sentences
graders.criteria: Judge the new skill's files. Instructions are plain sentences with concrete actions, not vague advice such as "investigate thoroughly" or "check the relevant logs".

graders.name: skill-file-exists
graders.description: The skill exists where the user asked.

graders.name: standalone
graders.criteria: Judge the new skill's files. The skill works with no other skill installed: any other skill it mentions is optional, or the steps that need it say what to do without it.

graders.name: state-changes-gated
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. It keeps the investigation read-only by default: database access only through `scripts/db-ro.sh`, and any action that changes production state (restarting or redeploying the ECS service, killing jobs, writing data, refunds) only after the user or on-call lead agrees. Any prohibition is paired with what to do instead (for example, propose the restart and its impact on in-flight webhooks, then wait).

graders.name: terminal-outcomes
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. It lets an investigation end more than one way and counts "no real problem" (false alarm, expected behavior, cannot reproduce) as a complete result, reported briefly with the evidence, alongside a confirmed cause and an open question that needs a person.

graders.name: time-sensitive-facts
graders.criteria: Judge `.agents/skills/investigate/SKILL.md`. Facts that change over time are not frozen as standing truth: it does not name who is on call, and a version fact such as "we're on Postgres 14" is either left out, stated with how to check it (for example `select version()`), or tied to the reason it matters. Pass if no on-call name and no unqualified current-version claim appear.
